claim: inferred from the CRM extract Files.zip (sha256 c66bae52) and the dell1 match sheet 20261016T0225Z (1)

methods.rule: exact equality of a sheet account with a published key after trimming and upper-casing, the sheet row HIGH with no conflict flag, and the household advisor equal to the sheet advisor; a certain direct link that grants HIGH

exact equality of a sheet account with the old account of a deterministic pair whose new account is a published key; the sheet row HIGH with no conflict flag and the household advisor equal to the sheet advisor; a certain link through a deterministic pair that grants HIGH

a deterministic pair gives the certain account-to-key link; an exact account number cited in the activity notes of exactly one household, at least twice, and in no other household's notes gives the certain household link; the household advisor must equal the portfolio advisor of that account (two independent sources agreeing); grants HIGH

a deterministic pair whose old account is cited in the notes under one household: MEDIUM where the pair list household or the sheet household names the same household (two independent sources agreeing), otherwise LOW; never grants access
an unconfirmed pair (to_confirm yes) whose old account is cited in the notes under one household is a candidate only, LOW at most; the unconfirmed pairs never grant access

notes: Words and counts only. The extract was read in memory from the nested zips; nothing was extracted to disk or into the repo, and the match table sits outside the repo. Linked: the 115 old pair accounts (all alphanumeric, none all-digit) appear as exact tokens in 138 activity rows naming 77 accounts; a row's regardingid resolved to a household by household id or by the contact's household id, and no row had an id in both spaces. Four published keys reached HIGH through a deterministic pair, a certain household and an advisor equal to the portfolio advisor (MX). Sheet direct and sheet-via-pair gave no HIGH link: no sheet account equals a published key, and no HIGH sheet row sits on a deterministic pair. The 107 unconfirmed pairs granted nothing and gave LOW candidates only (MY). Not linked: 877 keys have no household candidate and 58 are LOW. No published key appears as a token in any text member of the extract or in the imaging index, and the 870 directory account ids are opaque and none equals a published key, so for the large majority of the 939 keys no certain rule reaches the extract at all; only the 92 published keys on the pair list have a bridge, through the old account. The imaging index carries 78 of the 115 old accounts beside client names with no household id; names were not used as a link (CTO msg 10304 excludes fuzzy name matching). Advisors: the CRM names four household advisor codes; the Users table holds seven email addresses, but no certain key joins Users.UserID to a household advisor code (zero equal values), so no advisor email is joined and advisors_with_email is zero. Ambiguity ruled out: the sheet household cell resolved to a HouseholdID and HHID agreeing on one CRM row for 78 of 83 rows; the other five cells are blank or unpaired and grant nothing.
